title: Tensor preserves monomorphisms into residue-module sheaves
statement: Let C be a site with objects in Type(u+1), morphisms in Type(u), and essentially small in Type(u+1), with topology J. Let A be a commutative ring in Type(u+1), and let r in A generate a maximal ideal. For any monomorphism f:X to Y of sheaves of A-modules with r times id_Y zero, and any sheaf F of A-modules, f tensor id_F is a monomorphism. The tensor product is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor product; no section ring of the constant quotient field sheaf is assumed to be a field.

source.place: The field-tensor argument and finite scalar filtration, abstracted to the categorical hypotheses; see also Stacks more-algebra.tex, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent (Tag 0H75).

proof.text: The inclusion of sheaves into presheaves preserves monomorphisms. In each section, the target Y(U) is killed by r and hence has the canonical A/(r)-module structure. This is a vector space over a field, so it is semisimple as an A-module. Every monomorphism into it splits: extend the inverse from the image submodule to the whole module.

Tensoring a split monomorphism with F(U) remains split, so the sectionwise presheaf tensor map is monic. Exact sheafification preserves this monomorphism. The natural sheaf tensor comparison identifies its sheafification with f tensor id_F. The splittings need not be natural; only monicity is asserted sectionwise.
